summary: Re-ran and independently re-read every finding the fix report claims to have closed. All four blocker/major findings (ADV-L05-01 the hosted-census prestate abort, ADV-L05-02 the two invented length bounds, ADV-L05-03 the uncast acquired_date, ADV-L05-04 the self-feeding rate wall) are genuinely fixed on the current head: read the migration and runtime source directly rather than trusting the report's prose, and the exact code shapes the report describes are present (named 18-role roster + recorded-not-pinned count; count-both-windows-before-writing under the same advisory locks; no max on description with reason capped and clamped by the producer; calendarDay() throwing on a non-YYYY-MM-DD value). All eight minors (ADV-L05-05..08, SPEC-871-B/C, STD-1) are fixed and verified the same way (speaksFor/agreedOn shared across all three ground arms with residualCents removed; role-census-reset.test.mjs keyed on the file stem; roles-bootstrap.sql VERIFY census at 21; migration §D.T7b masking-drift guard; p871.door.five_states driving the roster, the signed-in preview and the new door for the same invite in all five states; the shared apps/web/components/registers/use-fa-particulars-proposal.ts hook wired into both entrances). Re-ran rather than trusted: pnpm typecheck (exit 0), CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint (exit 0), runtime unit fa-particulars-proposal-unit.test.mjs (24/24), runtime db-backed p871-invite-preview-db.test.mjs (9/9), check-frozen-workflows.mjs (OK, 312 files) and check-parts-parity.mjs (OK), all eight touched apps/web unit test files (46/46 across the files, 0 fail), and both browser walks on this lane's triple (members-invite-walk 7/7, depreciation-walk 5/5) — every number matches what wave4-lane05-fix.md claims. SPEC-871-A is correctly left open: the divergence from the re-brief's 'existing entry rate wall' wording still stands in the migration (0309 mints its own clara.invite_preview_attempts and never calls clara.claim_confirmation_attempt), and the fix report's own argument for why that is the right call rather than a defect still holds on re-reading — this is the owner's decision to make, not a lane defect, so it correctly stays open rather than being force-closed. One new, previously unflagged minor was found by the recheck itself (below) in the db test file's own literal probe tokens; it is a test-fixture fragility, not a functional regression — the production code it exercises was independently verified correct by direct source reading. Nothing above minor remains open.

findings.title: Two db rate-wall cells use fixed literal probe tokens, so re-running invite-preview-public.test.mjs against the same persistent lane database within 15 minutes of a prior run can flip a real assertion from not_previewable/preview to rate_limited
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/invite-preview-public.test.mjs:189 'const unknown = await previewByToken("f".repeat(64));' inside p871.door.no_oracle, and lines 574-576 'for (let i = 0; i < 4; i += 1) answers.push(await previewByToken(String(i).repeat(64), digest));' inside p871.wall.origin_limb, both hash to the SAME token_hash on every invocation. clara.invite_preview_attempts is append-only and unprunable (ADV-L05-04's own fix keeps it bounded at 5 rows per key per 15-minute window, never emptied). REPRODUCED LIVE: ran the touched gate-chain files once (70 tests, 69 pass, 1 skip — matches wave4-lane05-fix.md exactly), then ran the SAME command again about a minute later and got 2 failures: 'not ok 15 - p871.door.no_oracle ... {outcome:'rate_limited',retry_after_seconds:289}' vs expected {outcome:'not_previewable'}, and 'not ok 23 - p871.wall.origin_limb ... [rate_limited,rate_limited,rate_limited,rate_limited,preview]' vs expected the first four not_previewable. A direct query confirmed 5 rows for token_hash=sha256('f'.repeat(64)) inside the trailing 15-minute window at the moment of failure. A third run, after intervening typecheck/lint/unit gates had let the window age past 15 minutes, passed invite-preview-public.test.mjs clean at 16/16. Every OTHER rate-wall cell in the same file (p871.wall.bounded, p871.wall.no_slide, p871.wall.token_limb) already mints a fresh, real invite token per run via inviteMember() and is immune to this.
findings.required_fix: Replace the two fixed literals ('f'.repeat(64) at line 189, and String(i).repeat(64) for i in 0..3 at line 574) with a per-call-random 64-hex-char string (e.g. randomBytes(32).toString('hex')), the same way originDigest() already randomizes the address limb, so the two cells cannot collide with rows any earlier run of this file left behind on the shared lane database.

findings.title: SPEC-871-A remains genuinely open, correctly — not a defect in this round's fix, but not resolved either

The orchestrator/owner needs to rule on SPEC-871-A explicitly (ratify the divergence, or reopen #871) before this can be called fully closed — the fix report already frames the question correctly; carry it forward rather than re-litigate it here.
